newsitem.title: UK: Grade to quit UK's Channel 4 television.
newsitem.headline: Grade to quit UK's Channel 4 television.

text.p: Britain's Channel 4 television said on Monday its chief executive Michael Grade was quitting his post and would leave the industry.
Grade, 53, will step down in the next few months after agreeing terms of release from a five-year contract which had tied him into the company until June 2000.
"Michael Grade has told me he wishes to leave the television industry and pursue his other business interests," Channel 4's chairman Sir Michael Bishop said.
Grade agreed to pay the company about 105,000 pounds ($170,000) in compensation and gave the directors a legal undertaking not to compete with the network.

Grade, whose resignation took the world of British television by surprise, had headed the network since 1988, six years after it was founded as a public service corporation funded by the income from advertising.
The channel has a special remit to innovate and experiment and to appeal to tastes not generally catered for by the commercial ITV network.
As a result it has often come under fire in a public debate about broadcasting standards, with critics accusing it of putting out offensive, sexually explicit material.
Channel 4 said Grade's departure did not signal a change of direction for the network.
Bishop said: "Since 1988, Michael has directed Channel 4 with skill, determination and style.

"He has successfully steered the channel through its most testing period of transition in selling its own airtime, sustaining and enhancing the channel's unique programme remit and campaigning relentlessly on behalf of the company."
Grade, who fought off attempts to privatise the network, has maintained Channel 4's strong support for British cinema.
It was involved in the production of such recent hit films as "Four Weddings And A Funeral" and "Trainspotting".
Network chiefs will now consider candidates to replace Grade and Channel 4 finance director David Scott has in the meantime been promoted to the new position of managing director.

Grade, who comes from a prominent British showbusiness family, has previously been head of Light Entertainment at London Weekend Television, serving the capital, and controller of BBC1, the British Broadcasting Corporation's main television channel.
Grade is non-executive chairman of video distribution company VCI, which last year expressed an interest in buying Manchester United Football Club.
Industry experts said Grade would be hard to replace at Channel 4.
"He's given it incredible leadership," said Matt Baker, editor of Broadcast magazine.

"He defines the Channel. He's ebullient, aggressive, controversial, off-the-wall and very, very different from some of the rather grey characters who run some of the other television channels in this country."
Bishop said Grade had told him before Christmas that he wanted to leave the television industry where he had worked for 23 years. ($1=.6161 Pound)
